assessment.title: Homework #2 · Semiconductor physics and the pn junction
assessment.instructions: Assume T = 300 K unless stated: V_T = kT/q = 0.0259 V, n_i = 10¹⁰ cm⁻³, q = 1.602×10⁻¹⁹ C, μ_n = 1350 and μ_p = 480 cm²/V·s, ε_s = 11.7ε₀ ≈ 1.04×10⁻¹² F/cm. Einstein relation: D_n = μ_nV_T ≈ 35.0 cm²/s, D_p = μ_pV_T ≈ 12.4 cm²/s. Enter numbers in the units shown; scientific notation such as 2.93e-6 is accepted. Show each substitution and interpret signs.

questions.title: 1) Intrinsic silicon: conductivity and resistivity
questions.promptHtml:
Topic 2.1 · Intrinsic and doped semiconductors

Intrinsic Si at 300 K has n = p = ni = 1010 cm−3. Find σ and ρ, using σ = q(nμn + pμp).
hints: In intrinsic Si, n = p = n_i, so σ = q n_i (μ_n + μ_p).
checklist: Keep units in S/cm and Ω·cm.

questions.title: 2) n-type silicon: majority/minority carriers and ρ
questions.promptHtml: Given ND = 5×1015 cm−3 (no acceptors). Find n, then ρ. Also find the minority hole concentration p.
hints: N_D ≫ n_i, so complete ionization gives n ≈ N_D.
Mass-action law: np = n_i².
checklist: Drop the negligible hole term in σ.

questions.title: 3) Compensated doping
questions.promptHtml: Given ND = 1×1016 and NA = 3×1015 cm−3. Approximate n and p.
hints: Acceptors compensate donors: the net doping is N_D − N_A.
Then use np = n_i².

questions.title: 4) Electron drift current density
questions.promptHtml:
Topic 2.2 · Drift and diffusion currents

Given n = 1×1016 cm−3 and E = 10 V/cm. Find Jn,drift = qnμnE.
hints: Multiply out with q in coulombs; the result is in A/cm².
checklist: State the current direction relative to E.

responseFields.label: Direction of current and electron motion

studentRubric.label: Direction of current and electron motion

questions.title: 5) Electron diffusion current density from an exponential profile
questions.promptHtml: Let n(x) = n0e−x/L with n0 = 1016 cm−3 and L = 5 μm = 5×10−4 cm. Find Jn,diff at x = 0, using Jn,diff = qDn(dn/dx).
hints: dn/dx = −(n_0/L)e^(−x/L); evaluate at x = 0.
Use D_n ≈ 35.0 cm²/s from the Einstein relation.

questions.title: 6) Electric field needed to cancel diffusion (Jn = 0)
questions.promptHtml: At a point in silicon, (1/n)(dn/dx) = +150 cm−1. Find E such that Jn = qnμnE + qDn(dn/dx) = 0.
hints: Divide the zero-current condition by qnμ_n.
D_n/μ_n = V_T (Einstein relation).
checklist: Set J_n = 0 and solve for E.

questions.title: 7) Total electron current with both drift and diffusion
questions.promptHtml: Given n = 1015 cm−3, E = 5 V/cm, and dn/dx = −1018 cm−4. Compute Jn = qnμnE + qDn(dn/dx).
hints: Compute each term separately, then add with signs.
checklist: Signed sum; identify the dominant mechanism.

questions.title: 8) Built-in potential and depletion widths (equilibrium)
questions.promptHtml:
Topic 2.3 · pn junction

Abrupt pn junction with NA = 1017 and ND = 5×1015 cm−3. Find Vbi, W, xn, and xp.

Use Vbi = VT ln(NAND/ni2), W = √[(2εs/q)(1/NA + 1/ND)Vbi], and NAxp = NDxn.
hints: Report W, x_n and x_p in μm (1 μm = 10⁻⁴ cm).
x_n = W·N_A/(N_A+N_D) and x_p = W·N_D/(N_A+N_D).
checklist: Compute W in cm, convert to μm.
Identify which side the depletion region extends into.

responseFields.label: Which side holds most of W, and why?

questions.title: 9) Reverse bias: depletion width and junction capacitance
questions.promptHtml: Using the same junction, apply reverse bias VR = 5 V. Compute WR and the junction capacitance per unit area Cj,R, using WR = √[(2εs/q)(1/NA + 1/ND)(Vbi + VR)] and Cj = εs/W.
hints: W scales as √(V_bi + V_R).
C_j in F/cm² — report in nF/cm².
checklist: Compute C_j and compare with zero bias.

responseFields.label: How do W and C_j change with reverse bias?

questions.title: 10) Forward bias: minority-carrier injection at depletion edges
questions.promptHtml:
Using the same junction, apply forward bias VD = 0.30 V. Find the minority concentrations at the depletion edges:

pn(0) = pn0eVD/VT, with pn0 = ni2/ND;   np(0) = np0eVD/VT, with np0 = ni2/NA.
hints: The equilibrium minority concentrations come from mass action.

responseFields.label: Which side receives more injection, and is low-level injection valid?

questions.title: 11) Circuit Studio · Inside the pn junction: injection, r_d and the depletion region
questions.promptHtml:
Circuit Studio problem · Inside the device lens. Simulation tools are switched on for this question. Record each prediction before you use the tool that checks it.

A DC source VD is applied across a pn-junction diode with IS = 10 fA (entered as 0.01 pA), n = 1, VT = 25.85 mV.

  1. Predict: from ID = IS(eVD/VT − 1), compute ID at VD = 0.60 V.
  2. Open Edit circuit and choose Visual Aids ▾ → Inside the device, then click D1. Record ID and the local incremental resistance rd the lens reports.
  3. Select VD, change it to 0.66 V in the Edit tab, and record ID and rd again. Compute the voltage change per decade of current.
  4. Change VD to −2 V and watch the depletion region in the lens.
  5. Explain: (a) how the depletion region changed between forward and reverse bias, and why; (b) why a 60 mV step multiplies the current by about 10, using the injected minority-carrier concentration pn(0) = pn0eV/VT from Problem 10; (c) why rd = VT/ID fell by the same factor.
hints: The −1 term is negligible at these forward voltages.
Per decade of current, ΔV = nV_T·ln 10.
checklist: Lens readings recorded at 0.60 V and 0.66 V.
Injection explains both the current ratio and r_d.

responseFields.label: Voltage change per decade of current
Explain (a) depletion region, (b) injection and current ratio, (c) r_d
